No vocabulary finding (suprasellar mass, macroadenoma, histology sheets, visual field defect, etc.) is visibly shown or captioned; CK8 expression is not in allowed vocabulary, so panel excluded per findings rule. B: Panel B shows primary human NFPA cells with vimentin and Hoechst immunofluorescence as stated in caption and in-text. No vocabulary finding is visibly shown or captioned; vimentin expression is not in allowed vocabulary, so panel excluded per findings rule.

panels.figure_caption: (A) CK8 and Hoechst immunofluorescent staining; (B) Vimentin and Hoechst immunofluorescent staining. Magnification: × 400, scale bar: 100 μm.
in_text_mentions: Cytokeratins (CKs) are typically expressed in epithelial cells, whereas vimentin can be found in cells of mesenchymal origin. Co-expression of vimentin and CKs is believed to be the hallmark of epithelial-to-mesenchymal or mesenchymal-to-epithelial transformations of developing tissues. In this study, we analyzed the expression and co-expression of simple epithelial CK8 and vimentin in NFPA cells. The cells’ nuclei were stained with Hoechst 33342 dye, which emits a blue fluorescence, and CK8 and vimentin, which emit a green fluorescence (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E section of a patient pituitary adenoma showing large nuclei and clear heteromorphism, supporting atypical pituitary adenoma histology. B: Immunohistochemical specimen from patient pituitary adenoma showing low positive ACTH staining. C: Immunohistochemical specimen from patient pituitary adenoma showing negative growth hormone staining. D: Immunohistochemical specimen from patient pituitary adenoma showing negative prolactin staining.
